panels.rationale: Single axial contrast-enhanced CT (panel A) of a real patient from a case report whose title states brain metastasis secondary to primary vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma; in-text notes the intracranial mass was resected and histopathology confirmed metastasis from the vaginal clear cell carcinoma. The image shows a heterogeneously enhancing right parietal mass with a necrotic center, surrounding vasogenic edema and midline shift (annotated). No disease-specific CT vocabulary term exists for a brain metastatic deposit (the only CT term is pelvic mass), so the metastasis, necrosis, edema and midline shift are recorded as proposed findings. Brain metastasis is an uncommon (variant) presentation of vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial T2 MRI shows a right paraventricular/parietal brain mass with surrounding vasogenic edema and midline shift; the in-text mentions confirm this is metastasis from clear cell vaginal adenocarcinoma. No exact vocabulary finding matches this metastatic brain lesion, so the visible findings are proposed. B: Coronal T1 post-contrast MRI demonstrates a heterogeneously enhancing brain mass with a necrotic center and midline shift; in-text confirms metastasis from vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma. The specific findings are not represented in the supplied vocabulary. C: Sagittal T1 post-contrast MRI shows a heterogeneously enhancing parietal mass with surrounding vasogenic edema; in-text confirms this is metastatic vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma. Findings are proposed because the vocabulary lacks brain-metastasis descriptors.
